memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord heard you when you spoke to me, and the Lord said to me, "I have heard what this people said to you. Everything they said was good. Oh, that their hearts would be inclined to fear me and keep all my commands always, so that it might go well with them and their children forever!" - Deut 5:28-29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God's response is tender, almost aching with longing. He affirms that the people's words were good — they had spoken rightly about wanting to obey. But then comes that heartfelt cry: "Oh, that their hearts would be inclined to fear me and keep all my commands." God knew what they did not yet see: good intentions and right words are not the same as a changed heart. Israel meant well, but their hearts would soon wander.

This is the great problem the whole Old Testament exposes. People can promise obedience with their lips while their hearts remain unchanged. We know this in ourselves too — the gap between what we sincerely intend and what we actually do. God's longing here is for something deeper than external compliance. He wants hearts that truly love and reverence Him from within.

And this is exactly what the gospel provides. God did not leave His longing unanswered. Through the new covenant, He promised, "I will put my Spirit in you and move you to follow my decrees" (Ezek 36:26-27). What the law could reveal but not produce, the Holy Spirit now works within us. God's aching desire for hearts inclined toward Him is fulfilled in Christ, who gives us new hearts. If you long to obey but feel the weakness of your own heart, take courage — God Himself is at work in you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Where do I sense the gap between my good intentions and my actual obedience?
- Do I long for a heart that truly loves and reveres God, not just outward compliance?
- How does the promise of a new heart through the Spirit encourage me today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You long for hearts that truly love You, and You see how weak my own heart can be. Thank You for giving me a new heart through Your Spirit. Incline my heart to fear You and follow You always. Amen.
